title: "When to Hand Off, When to Work Together": Understanding Concurrent Human-Agent Interaction in Shared Co-Creative Workspaces
abstract: arXiv:2603.02050v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Shared co-creative workspaces allow users to contribute while agents execute. Yet how users adjust their participation as their work and the agent's execution shape one another remains less understood. We conducted two design probe studies with professional designers. In Study 1 (N=10), participants identified opportunities to contribute by observing the agent's progress, but avoided intervention when the agent misinterpreted their edits. Therefore, we developed CLEO, a second probe that tracks user actions and selectively updates its plan. In Study 2 (N=12), we analyzed 255 interaction turns and stimulated recall interviews, identifying five action categories, ten codes, six triggers, and four enabling factors. translated_title: “何时交接，何时协作”：理解共享共创工作空间中的人-智能体并发交互
translated_abstract: 共享共创工作空间允许用户在智能体执行任务的同时进行贡献。然而，随着用户的工作与智能体的执行相互塑造，用户如何调整自身的参与方式仍知之甚少。我们与专业设计师开展了两项设计探针研究。在研究1（N=10）中，参与者通过观察智能体的进展来识别贡献机会，但当智能体误解了他们的编辑时，他们会避免干预。因此，我们开发了CLEO——第二个探针，它能够追踪用户操作并有选择地更新其计划。在研究2（N=12）中，我们分析了255个交互回合及刺激性回忆访谈，识别出五类动作、十个编码、六种触发因素和四个促成因素。参与者在33.73%的回合中进行了并发交互，通过编辑表达新涌现的设计想法或偏好，并通过完成待处理的子任务或独立任务来改变工作分工。
tldr: 该研究通过与专业设计师的两项设计探针研究，揭示了共享共创工作空间中用户与智能体并发交互的模式与触发因素，并开发了能追踪用户操作、选择性更新计划的CLEO系统，为理解人机共创中的分工与协作提供了实证依据。
en_tdlr: Through two design probe studies with professional designers, this work reveals how users engage in concurrent interaction with agents in shared co-creative workspaces and introduces CLEO, a probe that tracks user actions and selectively updates its plan, identifying five action categories, six triggers, and four enabling factors.
